report.tagline: The UK's largest website and app for buying and selling new and used cars, where car dealers pay a monthly fee to list their stock.
report.simpleSummary: Auto Trader is where most people in the UK go to look for a car. You search by make, budget and distance, see hundreds of thousands of cars from dealers and private sellers, and contact the seller. Dealers pay Auto Trader a monthly subscription, about £3,000 on average, to put their cars in front of buyers. It started as a printed magazine in 1977, went fully online in 2013, and is now one of the most profitable companies on the London Stock Exchange.

overview.whatItDoes: Auto Trader runs a two-sided marketplace: car buyers search for free, and car sellers, mostly dealers, pay to list. It also sells dealers software and data tools, like pricing guidance and stock management, and earns from carmakers' ads and from leasing through Vanarama. It is led by CEO Nathan Coe and listed on the London Stock Exchange.
howItWorks: Dealers pay a monthly subscription based on how many cars they list and which package they choose.
Buyers search for free and see a price indicator ('Great price', 'Good price') based on Auto Trader's valuation data.
Buyers contact dealers, book test drives or use Deal Builder to reserve a car, value a part-exchange and arrange finance online.
Private sellers pay a one-off fee to list their car.
Dealers use Auto Trader's Portal software to price, manage and advertise stock.
Carmakers and finance companies pay for display ads and leads.
overview.valueProposition: For buyers: the biggest choice of cars in one place with fair-price guidance. For dealers: the most car buyers in the UK, so it is the one place they must list.

businessModel.summary: Auto Trader earns mostly from monthly dealer subscriptions. It raises revenue each year by adding products, raising prices and getting dealers to buy higher packages. Because it is mostly software, almost two-thirds of revenue is profit.

revenueStreams.detail: About £3,037 per forecourt per month across about 13,900 forecourts.
Private seller listing fees and finance or insurance referrals.
New car and van leasing; vehicle sales here fell 30%.

businessModel.pricing: Dealers pay monthly packages based on stock levels and product tier (not fully public); average about £3,037 per forecourt per month. Private sellers pay a one-off listing fee, typically from around £10 to £40 depending on package and car value. Buyers use it free.
costDrivers: Staff, especially engineers and data scientists
businessModel.unitEconomics: One dealer forecourt pays about £3,037 a month, or about £36,000 a year. Auto Trader keeps about 63% as operating profit, so roughly £23,000 per forecourt per year. Serving one more dealer costs very little because the website and audience already exist. For a dealer selling 20 cars a month, that is about £150 per car sold, which is why most still pay despite complaints.

howTheyGetUsers: Brand known since 1977 and top search results for car searches
Network effect: most cars bring most buyers
whatBringsUsersBack: Dealers need a steady flow of leads every month
Buyers come back when changing cars every few years
Dealer software built into daily work
growth.moat: Auto Trader has a powerful network effect: it has the most cars, so most buyers go there, so dealers must list there. Buyers spend 12 times more time on it than the next rival. Its price data from millions of listings is also hard to copy.

pmLessons: Moving early from print to digital let Auto Trader keep its leadership.
Network effects give pricing power, but pushing too hard angers customers.
Software margins can be very high when your marketplace is the default choice.
Adding transaction tools (Deal Builder) can deepen value but needs careful rollout.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Auto Trader's revenue without raising dealer prices?
interviewQuestions.hint: New products, consumer services, finance, ads. Measure ARPR and churn.

interviewQuestions.question: Dealers are angry about Deal Builder. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Listen, show data on sales, offer opt-in steps. Track adoption and churn.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Auto Trader with Cars24.
interviewQuestions.hint: Marketplace vs owning stock. Margins, risk, customer experience.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you use AI on Auto Trader?
interviewQuestions.hint: Smart search, pricing, lead scoring. Metrics: lead to sale rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Pick a north star metric.
interviewQuestions.hint: Cars sold via Auto Trader leads. Break into audience, stock, lead quality and dealer value.
